cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Make It Official
cards.instruction: Recruit someone by giving them a title, role, or ceremonial duty that makes participation feel binding.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Would you be honorary patron of our roof appeal? You'd open it and thank the donors.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can come, but I won't make a speech.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Then accept the patron's ribbon and lead the applause. That can be your ceremonial duty.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I leave after the first donation?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The patron applauds every donor. We couldn't have the later ones thinking their money mattered less.

mechanism: A treats limited help as qualifying service for an appointment A alone confers, then uses the role to make continuing participation feel obligatory.
confusable: D173 enforces an existing allocation; D175 recruits through newly conferred title or ceremonial duty, so A appointment itself must create the binding pressure.
comparison: Lantern holding becomes a successor-bound office; roof appeal substitutes ceremonial applause for refused public speaking and extends it to every donor.
seedUse: Read all four canonical seeds. Both Drive seeds contain actual role creation; assess whether A grants and defines participation rather than needing new ornamental rank sentences.
